name: coordinator-feedback-routing
body:
The coordinator-mediated feedback protocol — no Rust control flow changes, because the `apg review` subcommand surface is unchanged. It spans every prose surface that describes or drives the cycle:

- Distributed agent prompts (`opencode-suite/agents/*.md`). The `codebase-navigator` prompt gains the feedback-action grant (`apg_review_action`) and the prose: dispatch one feedback item at a time to one plan/spec/implementer writer, receive the writer's ACTIONED/WONT-FIX claim, perform a shallow consistency check (ACTIONED with no change, or WONT-FIX with changes, is inconsistent), then action the item (`apg_review_action --fix|--wont-fix`) or re-dispatch it, leaving the terminal resolve/reject to the reviewer. The writer prompts (spec-writer, plan-writer, and the generated implementer) drop the action grant, hold a read-only feedback channel (`apg_review` — the spec-writer and plan-writer gain the read channel; the implementer already has it), and state that the writer returns a claim and never actions. The reviewer prompts (spec-review, plan-review, implementation-phase-reviewer) keep add/resolve/reject, never action, and have their cycle diagrams re-pointed (today `spec-review.md` / `plan-review.md` show `writer: apg_review_action … → actioned`).
- Suite tool text (`opencode-suite/tools/apg_review_action.ts`): its description is re-pointed from the writer to the coordinator.
- This repo's generated agents (`.opencode/agents/implementer.md`, `.opencode/agents/implementation-phase-reviewer.md`), regenerated by agent-builder; the agent-builder template carries the same grant shape for the agents it scaffolds.
- Rust doc-comment wording describing the cycle: `src/review_cmd.rs`'s module doc (lines 1-5) and the `review_action` doc (lines 243-244) say the writer actions it; re-point to the coordinator. Behavior is unchanged — the `apg --help` header and the five-verb dispatch line stay as-is (pinned by `help_text_documents_strict_surface_and_preserves_review`), consistent with `requirements.requirement.review-surface-unchanged`.
- Repo docs describing the cycle (AGENTS.md / README.md "writer↔reviewer feedback cycle" wording), re-pointed at the coordinator-mediated cycle.

Agent prompts and tool text are not scanned code — they are embedded via `include_str!` and delivered by `apg init`, so the `implemented-by` spine anchors to the install/embed Rust and the review CLI action path, never to a `.md`/`.ts` path; the AGENTS.md/README wording is unscanned documentation and is likewise not an `implemented-by` target.
